chapter.name: Making of the Constitution
chapter.blurb: The demand for a Constituent Assembly, its composition and working, committees, enactment, enforcement and criticism.

source.title: Indian Polity (question set written from its topics)

questions.q: The idea of a Constituent Assembly for India was put forward for the first time in 1934. Who put it forward, and which body made the first official demand for it a year later?
questions.a: M.N. Roy; the Indian National Congress in 1935
questions.e: p.39: M.N. Roy first put forward the idea in 1934; the INC officially demanded an Assembly in 1935.
w: Nehru spoke in 1938, on behalf of the INC, of an Assembly on adult franchise; he did not originate the idea in 1934.
The Muslim League did not make the 1935 demand; it later wanted two Assemblies.
Cripps brought a British draft in 1942; he did not originate the idea.
o: M.N. Roy; the Indian National Congress in 1935
Jawaharlal Nehru; the Indian National Congress in 1935
M.N. Roy; the Muslim League in 1940
Sir Stafford Cripps; the Indian National Congress in 1938

questions.q: Which one of the following was accepted in principle by the British Government through the 'August Offer' of 1940?
questions.a: The demand for a Constituent Assembly to frame the Constitution of India
questions.e: p.39: the demand was finally accepted in principle by the British Government in the August Offer of 1940.
w: That was the Cabinet Mission scheme of 1946.
That was the Cripps draft proposal of 1942, which came after the August Offer.
The 1939 resolution was an act of the INC, not of the British Government.
o: The demand for a Constituent Assembly to frame the Constitution of India
The scheme for the Assembly that more or less satisfied the Muslim League
A draft proposal on the framing of an independent Constitution to be adopted after World War II
The Indian National Congress resolution of 1939 reiterating Nehru's view

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT a member of the Cabinet Mission that arrived in India on 24 March 1946?
questions.e: p.54, footnote 1: the Cabinet Mission consisted of Lord Pethick Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander. Nehru spoke for the INC in 1938 and was not on it.
w: Pethick Lawrence was a member of the Mission.
Cripps, who had come alone with a draft in 1942, was also a member of the 1946 Mission.
Alexander was the third member of the Mission.

questions.q: The Muslim League rejected the Cripps Proposals of 1942 because it wanted
questions.a: India divided into two autonomous states with two separate Constituent Assemblies
questions.e: p.39: the Cripps Proposals were rejected by the Muslim League, which wanted India divided into two autonomous states with two separate Constituent Assemblies.
w: The League sought two autonomous states, not one state with two Assemblies (p.39).
Adult franchise was the INC's 1938 demand, not the League's reason for rejection (p.39).
The text gives no such postponement demand; the reason was the two-state, two-Assembly demand (p.39).
o: India divided into two autonomous states with two separate Constituent Assemblies
India to remain one state, but with two separate Constituent Assemblies for the Hindu and Muslim communities
a single Constituent Assembly elected on the basis of adult franchise, as the Congress had demanded
the framing of the Constitution to be postponed until the princely states had agreed to join the Assembly

questions.q: Which one of the following is the correct chronological order of the events in the demand for the Constituent Assembly?
questions.a: Congress's official demand - August Offer - Cripps Proposals - Cabinet Mission
questions.e: p.39: INC demand 1935, August Offer 1940, Cripps 1942, then the Cabinet Mission (1946).
w: It puts the 1940 August Offer before the 1935 demand.
It puts the 1942 Cripps Proposals before the 1940 August Offer.
It puts the 1942 Cripps Proposals before the 1935 demand and the 1940 Offer after the Mission.
o: Congress's official demand - August Offer - Cripps Proposals - Cabinet Mission
August Offer - Congress's official demand - Cripps Proposals - Cabinet Mission
Congress's official demand - Cripps Proposals - August Offer - Cabinet Mission
Cripps Proposals - Congress's official demand - Cabinet Mission - August Offer

questions.q:
With reference to the declarations of the Indian National Congress on the Constituent Assembly, consider the following statements:

1. In 1938 Jawaharlal Nehru made his declaration on behalf of the Muslim League.
2. Nehru's 1938 declaration asked for an Assembly nominated by the provincial governments.
3. The INC passed a resolution in 1939 endorsing and reiterating the view of Nehru.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.39: he spoke on behalf of the INC. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.39: he asked for an Assembly elected on the basis of adult franchise. Statement 3 is correct: p.39.
w: '1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.39
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.39
'2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.39

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Sir Stafford Cripps and the British proposals of 1942:

1. Sir Stafford Cripps was the Viceroy of India when he brought the draft proposal.
2. He was a Member of the Cabinet when he came to India.
3. The Cripps Proposals were made in 1940, the same year as the August Offer.
4. His draft proposal concerned the framing of an independent Constitution to be adopted after World War II.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.39: he was a Member of the Cabinet who came with a draft proposal of the British Government; he was not the Viceroy. Statement 2 is correct: p.39. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.39: the August Offer was of 1940 and Cripps came in 1942. Statement 4 is correct: p.39.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.39
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.39
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.39

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Cabinet Mission of 1946:

1. It consisted of three members: Lord Pethick Lawrence, Sir Stafford Cripps and A.V. Alexander.
2. It arrived in India on 24 March 1946 and published its plan on 16 May 1946.
3. It accepted the Muslim League's demand for two separate Constituent Assemblies.
4. Its scheme for the Constituent Assembly more or less satisfied the Muslim League.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.54, footnote 1. Statement 2 is correct: p.54, footnote 1. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.39: it rejected the idea of two Assemblies. Statement 4 is correct: p.39.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.54
'1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.54
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.54

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the intervals between the events in the demand for a Constituent Assembly:

1. The INC's first official demand for an Assembly preceded the August Offer by four years.
2. M.N. Roy's idea of 1934 preceded the Cripps Proposals by eight years.
3. The INC resolution reiterating Nehru's view came one year before the August Offer.
4. Nehru's declaration of 1938 preceded the Cripps Proposals by three years.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.39: 1935 and 1940, an interval of five years. Statement 2 is correct: p.39: 1934 and 1942. Statement 3 is correct: p.39: 1939 and 1940. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.39: 1938 and 1942, an interval of four years.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.39
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.39
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.39

questions.q:
With reference to the Cabinet Mission and the events before it, consider the following statements:

1. The Cabinet Mission put forth a scheme for the Assembly that more or less satisfied the Muslim League.
2. The Cripps Proposals came before the Cabinet Mission was sent to India.
3. The Cabinet Mission accepted the idea of two separate Constituent Assemblies.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.39. Statement 2 is correct: p.39: 1942 and 1946. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.39: it rejected the idea of two Constituent Assemblies.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.39
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.39
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.39

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The idea of an Assembly was first put forward by the Indian National Congress.
2. The INC officially demanded a Constituent Assembly one year after the idea was first put forward.
3. M.N. Roy, who first put forward the idea, was a pioneer of the communist movement in India.
4. The Cripps Proposals came before the August Offer.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.39: it was put forward in 1934 by M.N. Roy; the INC demanded it officially in 1935. Statement 2 is correct: p.39: 1934 and 1935. Statement 3 is correct: p.39. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.39: the August Offer was of 1940 and the Cripps Proposals of 1942.
w: '2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.39
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.39
'3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.39

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the demand for a Constituent Assembly:

1. M.N. Roy, who first put forward the idea, was a pioneer of the communist movement in India.
2. The INC officially demanded a Constituent Assembly for the first time in 1938.
3. The British Government accepted the demand in full in the August Offer of 1940.
4. A Cabinet Mission was finally sent to India after the Cripps Proposals.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.39. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.39: the first official demand was in 1935; 1938 was Nehru's declaration. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.39: it accepted it only in principle. Statement 4 is correct: p.39.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.39
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.39
'4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.39

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the sequence of events in the demand for a Constituent Assembly:

1. The INC's first official demand for an Assembly came before Nehru's declaration on adult franchise.
2. The Cripps Proposals were made before the INC first officially demanded a Constituent Assembly.
3. M.N. Roy put forward the idea in the same year in which the INC first officially demanded it.
4. The Cripps Proposals were made after the INC passed its resolution of 1939.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.39: 1935 and 1938. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.39: the INC demanded it in 1935 and the Proposals came in 1942. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.39: Roy in 1934, the INC in 1935. Statement 4 is correct: p.39.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.39
'1 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.39
'4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.39

questions.q:
With reference to the Congress declaration of 1938, consider the following statements:

1. It insisted that the Constitution of free India must be framed without outside interference.
2. It came after the INC had first officially demanded a Constituent Assembly in 1935.
3. It was reiterated by the INC through a resolution in 1939.
4. It wanted the Assembly to be elected on the basis of adult franchise.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.39. Statement 2 is correct: p.39: 1935 and 1938. Statement 3 is correct: p.39. Statement 4 is correct: p.39.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.39
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.39
'1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.39

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The INC for the first time officially demanded a Constituent Assembly in 1938.
2. Nehru made his declaration on adult franchise after the Cripps Proposals were made.
3. The Cripps Proposals and the Cabinet Mission came in the same year.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.39: in 1935; 1938 was Nehru's declaration. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.39: his declaration was in 1938, the Proposals in 1942. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.39 and p.54, footnote 1: 1942 and 1946. So none of them are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: none is correct.
'Only two' miscounts: none is correct.
'All three' miscounts: none is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. Sir Stafford Cripps came to India in 1942 with a draft proposal of the British Government.
2. The Cabinet Mission rejected the idea of two Constituent Assemblies.
3. The INC officially demanded a Constituent Assembly for the first time in 1935.
4. The Cripps Proposals came two years after the August Offer.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.39. Statement 2 is correct: p.39. Statement 3 is correct: p.39. Statement 4 is correct: p.39: 1940 and 1942. So exactly 4 are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 4 are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 4 are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 4 are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. Sir Stafford Cripps was a Member of the Cabinet when he came to India with his draft proposal.
2. The INC officially demanded a Constituent Assembly in 1934.
3. The Cabinet Mission was sent to India before the Cripps Proposals.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.39. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.39: in 1935; 1934 was Roy's idea. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.39: the Mission came last, in 1946, after the Proposals of 1942. So exactly 1 are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct (statements 1).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct (statements 1).
'All three' miscounts: exactly 1 are correct (statements 1).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Muslim League rejected the Cripps Proposals of 1942.
Statement-II: The League wanted India divided into two autonomous states with two separate Constituent Assemblies.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: p.39. Statement-II is correct: p.39, and it is the League's reason for rejecting the Proposals.
w: Rejected: Statement-II is the very reason for the rejection, so it does explain Statement-I.
Rejected: Statement-II is correct (p.39).
Rejected: Statement-I is correct (p.39).
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Cabinet Mission rejected the idea of two separate Constituent Assemblies.
Statement-II: The Cabinet Mission put forth a scheme for the Assembly which more or less satisfied the Muslim League.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: p.39. Statement-II is correct: p.39, but it is a separate feature of the Mission's work and does not explain why it rejected two Assemblies.
w: Rejected: the page gives the satisfying scheme as a separate step; it does not account for the rejection of two Assemblies.
Rejected: Statement-II is correct (p.39), so the pair is not 'I correct, II incorrect'.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct (p.39), so the pair is not 'I incorrect'.
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct

questions.q:
Match the event in List-I with its year in List-II.

List-I
A. M.N. Roy puts forward the idea of a Constituent Assembly
B. The INC officially demands a Constituent Assembly
C. The August Offer
D. The Cripps Proposals

List-II
1. 1935
2. 1942
3. 1940
4. 1934
questions.e: p.39: Roy 1934, INC 1935, August Offer 1940, Cripps 1942.
w: A and B are interchanged.
C and D are interchanged.
Both pairs are interchanged.

questions.q: Under the Cabinet Mission Plan the total strength of the Constituent Assembly was to be 389. How many of these seats were allotted to British India?
questions.e: p.39: 389 in all; 296 for British India and 93 for the princely states. (292 was only the governors' provinces share.)
w: 292 was the share of the eleven governors' provinces; four more came from Chief Commissioners' provinces.
93 was the princely states' share.
299 was the strength after partition (pp.41-42).

questions.q: The representatives of each community in the Constituent Assembly were elected by the members of that community in the provincial legislative assembly by
questions.a: proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote
questions.e: p.39: the representatives of each community were elected by members of that community in the provincial legislative assembly, voting being by proportional representation by means of single transferable vote.
w: The scheme named proportional representation by single transferable vote, not first-past-the-post (p.39).
Each community's members elected its own representatives; the whole house did not vote together (p.39).
The method was the single transferable vote, not a party-list system (p.39).
o: proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote
the first-past-the-post method in single-member constituencies
a simple majority vote of the whole provincial assembly, irrespective of community
proportional representation by the list system, with seats shared among parties

questions.q: Which one of the following best describes the Constituent Assembly constituted in November 1946?
questions.a: A partly elected and partly nominated body whose members were indirectly elected
questions.e: pp.39-40: states' members were nominated by their heads; British India's members were elected by provincial assemblies, which were elected on a limited franchise.
w: The text says it was not directly elected on adult franchise.
British India's members were elected by the provincial assemblies, not nominated by the Viceroy.
The princely states' representatives were nominated by their heads, not elected by state legislatures.
o: A partly elected and partly nominated body whose members were indirectly elected
A body elected directly by the people of India on the basis of adult franchise
A body all of whose members were nominated by the Viceroy of India
A body elected by the provincial assemblies and by the legislatures of the princely states

questions.q: Which one of the following important personalities of that time was NOT a member of the Constituent Assembly?
questions.e: p.40: the Assembly included all important personalities of India at that time, with the exception of Mahatma Gandhi.
w: Nehru chaired three major committees and moved the Objectives Resolution (pp.40, 42).
Patel chaired the Provincial Constitution Committee (p.42).
Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee (p.43).

questions.q: In the elections of July-August 1946 to the 296 seats of British India, the Indian National Congress won 208 seats. How many seats did the Muslim League win?
questions.e: p.40 and Table 2.2 (pp.47-48): Congress 208, Muslim League 73, small groups and independents 15.
w: 80 is the strength of Muslims in the community-wise Table 2.3, not the League's seats.
93 is the seats of the princely states, which were not filled.
15 is what the small groups and independents got.

questions.q:
With reference to the composition of the Constituent Assembly under the Cabinet Mission Plan, consider the following statements:

1. The total strength was 389, of which 296 seats went to British India and 93 to the princely states.
2. The 296 British Indian seats included 292 from the eleven governors' provinces and four from the Chief Commissioners' provinces.
3. Seats were allotted to provinces and states roughly at one for every million of population.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.39. Statement 2 is correct: p.39. Statement 3 is correct: p.39.
w: '2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.39
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.39
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.39

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the allotment of seats under the Cabinet Mission scheme:

1. Seats of each British province were divided between two principal communities, Hindus and Muslims.
2. 'General' meant all except Muslims and Sikhs.
3. Each province and princely state, or group of states in the case of small states, was allotted seats in proportion to its population.
4. The provinces received equal numbers of seats, irrespective of population.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.39: three principal communities - Muslims, Sikhs and General. Statement 2 is correct: p.39. Statement 3 is correct: p.39. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.39: seats were in proportion to population.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.39
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.39
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect: p.39

questions.q:
With reference to the election of the British Indian members of the Constituent Assembly, consider the following statements:

1. The provincial assemblies that elected them had themselves been elected on the basis of adult franchise.
2. The members were indirectly elected by the members of the provincial assemblies.
3. The representatives of a community were elected by all the voters of that community in the province.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.40: they were elected on a limited franchise. Statement 2 is correct: p.40. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.39: they were elected by the members of that community in the provincial legislative assembly.
w: '1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.40
'3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.40
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect: p.40

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the elections to the Constituent Assembly:

1. The elections for the 296 British Indian seats were held in 1947.
2. The elections for the British Indian seats were held after the Cabinet Mission had published its plan.
3. The 93 seats of the princely states were filled at the outset of the elections.
4. The small groups and independents got the remaining 15 seats.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.40: they were held in July-August 1946. Statement 2 is correct: p.54 footnote 1 and p.40: plan on 16 May 1946; elections in July-August 1946. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.40: they were not filled as the states stayed away. Statement 4 is correct: p.40.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct: p.40
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.40
'4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.40

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the provinces of 1946 (footnotes 2 and 3):

1. Coorg was one of the eleven governors' provinces.
2. Sindh was one of the four Chief Commissioners' provinces.
3. British Baluchistan was one of the four Chief Commissioners' provinces.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: p.54, footnote 3: Coorg was a Chief Commissioners' province. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.54, footnote 2: Sindh was a governors' province. Statement 3 is correct: p.54, footnote 3.
w: '2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.54
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.54
'1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.54

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the character of the Constituent Assembly:

1. It comprised representatives of Hindus, Muslims, Sikhs, Parsis, Anglo-Indians, Indian Christians, SCs and STs, including women.
2. It was not directly elected by the people of India on the basis of adult franchise.
3. Its British Indian members were nominated by the Viceroy.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.40. Statement 2 is correct: p.40. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.40: they were elected by members of the provincial assemblies.
w: '2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.40
'1 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.40
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.40

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the allotment of the 389 seats:

1. Small princely states could be grouped together to share seats.
2. The eleven governors' provinces together were allotted 296 seats.
3. The scheme reserved seats for the Congress and the Muslim League as parties.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.39: 'group of states in case of small states'. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.39: they had 292; 296 is the share of all British India, with the four Chief Commissioners' provinces. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.39-40: seats went to provinces, states and communities; the party figures are election results.
w: '2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.39
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.39
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect: p.39

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. In the case of small states, a group of states could be allotted seats together.
2. The Constituent Assembly was formed under the scheme of the Cabinet Mission Plan.
3. The 93 seats of the princely states were over one-third of the Assembly's total strength of 389.
4. One seat was allotted to each of the four Chief Commissioners' provinces.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.39. Statement 2 is correct: p.39. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.39: 93 of 389 is about one-quarter. Statement 4 is correct: p.39.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct: p.39
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.39
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.39

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The representatives of each community were elected only by the members of that community in the provincial legislative assembly.
2. The total strength of the Assembly under the scheme was 296.
3. The single transferable vote is the method of proportional representation named in the scheme.
4. The princely states' representatives had to be chosen on the basis of population by election.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.39. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.39: the total was 389; 296 was the share of British India. Statement 3 is correct: p.39. Statement 4 is incorrect: p.40: nominated by their heads.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct: p.39
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: p.39
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: p.39

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The total strength of the Assembly under the Cabinet Mission Plan was 389.
2. The four Chief Commissioners' provinces together had 292 seats.
3. Each of the four Chief Commissioners' provinces was allotted one seat.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.39. Statement 2 is incorrect: p.39: 292 was for the governors' provinces; the four provinces had one seat each. Statement 3 is correct: p.39. So exactly 2 are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 3).
'All three' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 3).
'None' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 3).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The elections for the 296 British Indian seats were held in July-August 1946.
2. The princely states' representatives were nominated by the heads of the states.
3. Mahatma Gandhi was a member of the Assembly.
4. The small groups and independents together got 15 seats.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: p.40. Statement 2 is correct: p.40. Statement 3 is incorrect: p.40: the Assembly included all important personalities of the time except Mahatma Gandhi. Statement 4 is correct: p.40. So exactly 3 are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 4).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 4).
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 4).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Assembly had 15 women members.
2. Delhi was one of the eleven governors' provinces.
